title: The Go SDK's direct (legacy) ZDX client: credentials, sign-in, retries and limits, and why the ZDX services do not use it

prose.text: Besides the OneAPI client, the Go SDK ships a ZDX client that signs in with a ZDX API key against the direct ZDX host. Its settings matter only for calls that actually go through it.

prose.label: Retries.
prose.text: {{reauth}} {{retry-defaults}} {{backoff}} {{retry-exhaustion}} The 5xx classification shared by all Go clients is in [[shared.sdk-go.retries:shared-5xx-classifier]].

checks.do: Whether the Go program built a OneAPI service or a legacy ZDX service: the ZDX service functions fail on a legacy service that has no ZPA client.
Whether request pacing was expected from the 100-per-minute limiter, which throttles only the sign-in call.

env-and-host.statement: The Go ZDX client reads `ZDX_API_KEY_ID`, `ZDX_API_SECRET` and `ZDX_CLOUD`, and uses `https://api.zdxcloud.net` by default or the `https://api.%s.net` pattern filled with a named cloud.

token-request.statement: It posts the sign-in to the base URL plus `/v1/oauth/token`, with the key ID, the current Unix timestamp and a key secret computed as the hex SHA-256 of the API secret, a colon and the timestamp.

token-expiry.statement: Before each request it signs in again when it has no token or the token has expired.

partner-header.statement: A partner ID from `ZSCALER_PARTNER_ID` (or the setter) is sent on each request as the `x-partner-id` header.

reauth.statement: On an unauthorized or forbidden response the client calls `Authenticate` again and retries the original request once; `Authenticate` requests a new token only when the cached one is missing, empty or expired, and otherwise returns the cached token.

quotes: if _, err := Authenticate(ctx, config, config.Logger); err != nil { client.Config.Logger.Printf("[ERROR] Re-authentication failed: %v", err)
resp, err = client.do(req, v, start, reqID)

evidence.after: func Authenticate(ctx context.Context, cfg *Configuration, logger logger.Logger) (*AuthToken, error) {

retry-defaults.statement: Requests go through a retrying HTTP client whose defaults are 100 retries with waits of 5 to 20 seconds, and a maximum-retries setting of 0 means retrying without a practical limit (`math.MaxInt32`).

backoff.statement: Its backoff reads `X-Ratelimit-Remaining-Second` and `X-Ratelimit-Limit-Second`, waits 1 second plus jitter when fewer than the threshold (2 by default) requests remain, waits 2 seconds after a 429, and otherwise backs off exponentially.

quotes: l.Printf("[WARN] 429 received, applying fallback retry delay (2s)")
// Use exponential backoff for all retries

retry-exhaustion.statement: When the retry budget runs out without a transport error, the client returns the last API response instead of a bare give-up error.

quotes: // err is nil only when the retry budget ran out while CheckRetry still

l.Printf("[WARN] giving up after %d attempt(s); surfacing API response status %d", numTries, resp.StatusCode)

global-limiter.statement: The client's configuration installs a global limiter of 100 requests per 60 seconds with an additional 5-second delay on `cfg.HTTPClient`, the client the sign-in request uses; each API request instead builds a fresh retrying client with `getHTTPClient` and no rate limiter, whose transport is a plain `http.Transport`.

limiter-auth-only.statement: So the fixed 100-per-60-seconds limiter paces only sign-in requests; API calls through this client are paced only by the header-driven backoff and the server's limits.
limiter-auth-only.conditions: Read from where each HTTP client is used at the pin; `getHTTPClient` never references its rate-limiter argument.

service-routing.statement: The ZDX service functions call `service.Client.NewRequestDo`, which on a service configured for legacy clients forwards to the legacy ZPA client and fails with 'legacy client is not set' when that client is nil; the function that forwards to the legacy ZDX client is `NewZdxRequestDo`.

quotes: resp, err := service.Client.NewRequestDo(ctx, "POST", path, nil, payload, &response)
var errLegacyClientNotSet = fmt.Errorf("legacy client is not set")
func (client *Client) NewZdxRequestDo(ctx context.Context, method, endpoint string, options, body, v interface{}) (*http.Response, error) {
return client.oauth2Credentials.LegacyClient.ZdxClient.NewRequestDo(ctx, method, removeOneApiEndpointPrefix(endpoint), options, body, v)

services-not-routed.statement: So a service built with `NewLegacyZdxClient` cannot run the ZDX service functions: they reach the missing legacy ZPA client and return an error, and the direct ZDX client's sign-in, retries and limiter never apply to them; the SDK's ZDX example builds a OneAPI service instead.
services-not-routed.conditions: A search of `zscaler/zdx/services` at the pin finds every ZDX service function calling `service.Client.NewRequestDo` and none calling `NewZdxRequestDo`, which only a unit test calls; not run against a tenant.
